cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is carrying the good news from city to city. Now he leaves Athens and goes to Corinth, where he finds a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, and his wife Priscilla. They've just come from Italy, and trust me, friend, they did NOT leave Rome for a vacation.

cards.question: Why did Aquila and Priscilla have to leave Rome?

answers.text: Claudius ordered all Jews out of Rome
A famine struck the whole city
A fire burned down their home

cards.text: Paul goes to visit them, and he ends up staying and working with them. Friend, if I ever met somebody out here who did what I do, I would NEVER leave either.

cards.question: Paul stays and works with Aquila and Priscilla because they're ___ by trade, just as he is.

cards.text: So Paul's got a day job now. But every Sabbath, he's in the synagogue, reasoning with people and trying to persuade them.

cards.question: Every Sabbath in the synagogue, Paul tries to persuade only the Jews.

cards.text: Then Silas and Timothy, Paul's traveling partners, come down from Macedonia. Backup has ARRIVED, and Paul devotes himself fully to the word.

cards.question: Now Paul testifies to the Jews that Jesus is ___.

cards.text: But they oppose him and insult him. So Paul shakes out his garments and tells them, "Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it."

cards.question: After the insults, who does Paul say he'll go to from now on?
So Paul walks out of the synagogue. Where does he go?

cards.text: Titus Justus, a worshiper of God, lives NEXT DOOR to the synagogue. That's like quitting your job and setting up your desk in the company parking lot.
Now, the leader of that synagogue is a man named Crispus. I bet the whole synagogue is holding its breath on this one.

cards.question: Crispus, the synagogue leader, believes in the Lord, along with his whole household.
And many of the Corinthians who hear the message believe and are ___.

cards.text: Paul's been opposed and insulted in this city. Then one night, the Lord speaks to him in a vision.

cards.question: The Lord tells Paul, "Do not be ___; keep on speaking; do not be silent."

cards.text: Keep on speaking. Do not be silent. Friend, NOBODY has ever had to tell me that twice.

cards.question: The Lord says He is with Paul, and no one will lay a hand on him, because He has many ___ in this city.
So Paul stays in Corinth, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians. For how long?

cards.text: A YEAR AND A HALF of teaching. Then, while Gallio is proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinate an attack on Paul.
"This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law," they say. Paul's ready, mouth open, first word loading.

cards.question: Paul gets to make his defense before Gallio.

cards.text: Just as Paul is about to speak, Gallio cuts in. He tells the Jews that if this were a wrongdoing or vicious crime, it would be reasonable to hear their complaint.

cards.question: Gallio says this isn't a crime. What does he call it instead?

answers.text: A dispute about words and their own law
A plot to stir up a revolt in the city
An insult against the honor of Caesar

cards.question: Gallio agrees to judge the case himself.

cards.text: And Gallio drives them away from the judgment seat. Paul never got a single word in, and the case STILL went his way.

cards.question: Then the crowd seizes a man and beats him right in front of the judgment seat. Who is it?
Gallio steps in to stop the crowd from beating Sosthenes.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 2 quotes "Do not be ___; keep on speaking; do not be silent.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Claudius first appears in the right answer, and no card ever says who he is (emperor of Rome). The baker is left with a name and no idea why he could order the Jews out of Rome.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 5 says only that Paul reasons with "people" in the synagogue. Nothing tells the baker that Greeks are there too, so the true/false pick is a coin flip. Stop 1 already has several discovery questions (cards 2, 4 and 11), so this one should be given context. For example, card 5 could mention who is in the synagogue, or the card could ask something the baker can reason out.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: "Backup has ARRIVED, and Paul devotes himself fully to the word" presents Silas and Timothy's arrival as the reason Paul devotes himself fully to the word. Acts 18:5 only says it happened "when" they came. It doesn't say how the two things connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer "the Christ" is a title with an article. The wrong answers "Elijah" and "Moses" are bare personal names, so the right answer stands out by its form. "Moses" is also barely believable as something Paul would testify Jesus is.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question asks "who" Paul will go to. Only "To the Gentiles" names a people. "Back to Jerusalem" and "On to Macedonia" are places and don't answer a "who" question, so the right answer gives itself away.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This card only repeats "Keep on speaking. Do not be silent." from verse 9, which the baker just saw in card 2's question, and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: "Where do they bring Paul?" uses "they" to point back to card 6, which is no longer on screen. The question should say who brings him (the Jews who attack Paul) and what is happening.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card cites only Acts 18:13. Its line "Paul's ready, mouth open, first word loading" tells that Paul was about to speak, which comes from Acts 18:14. The citation should be Acts 18:13-14.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 10 and this question both say the matter isn't a crime. Both wrong answers ("A plot to stir up a revolt in the city" and "An insult against the honor of Caesar") are crimes, so the setup rules them out and leaves only the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 1 states facts from outside the passage: Paul is "an apostle of Jesus," "carrying the good news from city to city." Stop 1 card 7 does the same with Silas and Timothy as "Paul's traveling partners." The docs say outside facts need their reference. But a story card has only one "verses" field, and it must cite the passage verses the card tells, "no wider and no narrower." There is no place to put the outside reference.
findings.question: When a story card states a fact from outside the passage (like who Paul or Silas and Timothy are), where should that fact's reference go? Should it be added to the card's "verses" field, put in the card text, or left off for simple introductions of who someone is?
